findings.title: A cell declaring role ceiling takes the session model and is invisible to the 40 percent escalation ration
findings.detail: Corroborated by three reviewers independently — security and code-quality traced it, test-coverage executed it. prepare.rs:941 reads `else if escalated_cell || tier_token == ESCALATION_WORD`, and on the from_role path tier_token IS the cell's own declared role string, so the arm fires before resolve_role_named is ever called: Resolved::Inherit, channel session-model, no model param. Meanwhile cell_is_escalated (validate.rs:98) reads only escalate==true or the legacy tier==ceiling, so the same record is invisible to all three counters that enforce D5 — escalation_share_after (handlers_close.rs:1113), role_mix (status_full/cells.rs:622) and ceiling_scarcity_warning (session_preamble/store.rs:314). Executed proof on a 7-cell feature with six such cells: model=None, channel=session-model, cell_is_escalated=false, and set_escalation on the seventh was ALLOWED at 86 percent escalated. Two things make this a door rather than an oversight: cells/tests.rs asserts role ceiling is accepted at add time, and models.rs:530-538 carries a comment stating the opposite of what ships — that such a cell warns and falls through like any other. D5 locks the ration as unchanged in force and plan.md:187 rates it HIGH with the proof that the 40 percent refusal fires on the flag exactly as on the tier value. It does, and is bypassable around it. No test connects add-time acceptance to the dispatch interception.
findings.fix: Either refuse ceiling in the role field at validate.rs:252 (the reserved-name option CONTEXT.md:154 already contemplated), or narrow prepare.rs:941 so a cell role falls through the resolver exactly as models.rs:530-538 promises. Whichever is chosen, add the test that connects the two layers, and correct the comment.
findings.evidence: verbs/drivers/prepare.rs:941; verbs/cells/validate.rs:98,252; verbs/cells/handlers_close.rs:1113; verbs/status_full/cells.rs:622; hooks/session_preamble/store.rs:314; verbs/drivers/models.rs:530-538

findings.title: cells backfill-roles scans outside its lock, so a concurrent write is silently overwritten by the pre-scan snapshot
findings.detail: Corroborated by two reviewers — code-quality traced the mechanism, test-coverage demonstrated the loss and raised it from P2. The verb reads every cell at handlers_write.rs:1537 to build its plan, takes the cells-archive lock only at :1607, then writes each whole object back with write_json_atomic at :1613. The lock therefore guards the write phase alone; the scan is unlocked, and every write is a full-object write of a stale clone. Demonstrated on a 40000-cell tempfile store: a real operator door — set_escalation with --off, which is not budget-checked and so performs no store scan — committed a disarm to disk at t=25ms; the backfill finished at t=1.007s and the cell was re-armed on disk, escalate=true. The operator's write was not half-applied, it was fully applied and then fully reversed. The doc block at :1523-1531 asserts the opposite: that a concurrent cells update, cap or claim cannot half-write behind this pass. A budget-checked --on attempt was correctly refused by the lock at 319ms, which is why the defect is invisible to casual testing: only writers completing inside the scan phase are lost. Code-quality additionally traced that a bee close archiving a feature during the scan is not blocked, and the subsequent write recreates .bee/cells/<id>.json as a live duplicate, because read_cell prefers the live copy. Severity is P1 rather than P2 because the loss is silent, the verb has not yet been run against the live 543-cell store, and this repository's stated default is concurrent sessions — main gained commits from a sibling session twice during this feature's own development.
findings.fix: Take the cells-archive lock before the scan so one lock spans scan and write, or re-read each file under the lock and merge only the three keys the migration owns (role, escalate, trace.escalation_reason) rather than writing the snapshot. Then pin it: hold the lock externally and assert the verb refuses, or mutate a record mid-pass and assert the operator write survives. Falls to P2 only if the migration is run under a documented single-session stop-the-world.
findings.evidence: verbs/cells/handlers_write.rs:1523-1531 (the claim), :1537 (unlocked scan), :1607 (lock), :1613 (whole-object write); verbs/drivers/guard.rs:325-331 (read_cell prefers the live copy)

findings.title: A null-valued role slot reopened the unconfigured-advisor P2 one input later — found by the delta pass, fixed in a7338b24
findings.detail: The delta re-review found that c2ef2f9f closed the ABSENT case and left the NULL case. known_roles derived from table.keys(), and a key whose value is null is still a key, so models.claude.advisor = null admitted the marker and inherited the session model while --role advisor refused on the same host. Reachable by the documented configuration: bee's own .bee/config-sample.json teaches null as the off spelling for advisor. Third instance of null-versus-absent in this feature. Fixed in a7338b24 by role_is_declarable, which decides the question ONCE by asking whether the resolution a dispatch would actually perform yields something, rather than testing the key or the value. Worth recording for whoever reads this later: the obvious fix, refusing any null-valued key, would have emptied known_roles on codex, whose default_models seeds every slot null, denying every codex dispatch. The worker found that before writing it.
findings.fix: Shipped in a7338b24 with the F3 predicate unification (both doors ask known_role_named, case-insensitive, answering in the config spelling), the F4 documentation correction in onboard/templates.rs, and the F6 derived FIX text.
findings.evidence: verbs/drivers/guard.rs role_is_declarable; hooks/model_guard.rs classify_marker; verbs/drivers/prepare.rs known_role_named; .bee/config-sample.json advisor null spelling

decision.review: Panel of four over a frozen 36-commit diff, then a delta pass over the fixes. 23 findings at first synthesis — P1 2, P2 7, P3 14. No reviewer filed a P1 alone; both P1s were corroboration promotions that were then executed rather than left as traces. P1-A (a cell declaring role ceiling took the session model, uncounted by the 40 percent ration) fixed by mrs-30 in commit 06e95097, with a two-layer test checked red first. P1-B (cells backfill-roles scanned outside its lock and fully reversed a concurrent operator write) fixed by mrs-31 in commit 00fd53b6, with a scan/lock seam so the race is pinned deterministically rather than by timing. The guard pair fixed in c2ef2f9f, and the delta pass caught that fix leaving its null-valued twin open — closed in a7338b24. The delta sweep showed the lock class was a genuine outlier by enumerating every other read-then-write in scope, and that the word-means-two-things class is where the siblings live. Three P3s filed to the backlog with fix directions: a ceiling key that now fails closed, a backfill report counting on two clocks, and an unlocked keep-set read in worker prune that predates this feature. Suite at approval: 2659 unit tests and 25 targets green, with three known exceptions each verified rather than assumed — two OpenCode tests that refuse to report green without a TypeScript-capable node, the binary_freshness flake, and a pre-existing claim-file race diagnosed and fixed by a sibling session. Owner approved merge 2026-08-25.
